rationale: Both miss most ground-truth concerns (slot-leak on abort, ceil-division bug in audio_tokenizer_v2.py:949, v2-tokenizer/legacy-checkpoint mismatch, docstring/provenance issues, WER-fallback raw-bytes skew, cleanup/generalizability questions), so recall is low for both. X's headline 'blocker' (put_req_chunk never incremented) is repeated as two separate findings and looks like a false positive — Y specifically investigated the same code and found it's a framework-managed counter matching qwen3_tts.py/fish_speech.py's pattern, which tanks X's precision since its top-billed findings are likely wrong; X's generator= finding is also explicitly hedged ('not read in full'), further hurting grounding. Y's findings (test-coverage gap, max_new_frames scalar-tolerance regression matching a cited sibling-line comparison, dead ref-codes, ignored sampler params, load_weights fragility) are more specific and better cited, though Y also confidently and wrongly clears the actual High-severity slot-leak bug as 'handled' — a serious false-negative dressed as verification, since that bug was real and later fixed by the author. On balance Y's findings are more trustworthy and actionable despite its own dangerous false-clear, edging out X's fabricated blocker.
